skill.name: AgentDB Learning Plugins
skill.description: Build and train AgentDB learning plugins for reinforcement learning workflows, including Decision Transformer, Q-Learning, SARSA, Actor-Critic, active learning, and related techniques.
skill.summary: Scaffold, train, and evaluate AgentDB reinforcement learning plugins.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown code fence false positives, not Ruby shell execution. The confirmed risks are npx examples that can execute remote npm package code and a local AgentDB SQLite data path that may store sensitive experiences. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin AgentDB package versions in all commands and ask users to review npm package provenance before execution.

remediation.issue: Local learning database may contain sensitive experiences
remediation.suggestion: Document data handling requirements, add .agentdb/ to ignore lists, and advise users to remove credentials before storage.
Clarify which commands are optional user actions and warn that the skill does not run them automatically.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable ways to build learning agents without rebuilding reinforcement learning scaffolding. This skill guides AgentDB plugin creation, training, evaluation, and algorithm selection.
actual_capabilities: Creates AgentDB plugin workflows with CLI examples for templates and inspection.
Explains nine learning algorithms and the cases where each is useful.
Shows how to store experiences, train models, and evaluate suggested actions.
Covers experience replay, prioritized replay, and incremental training patterns.
Connects trained learning models with AgentDB reasoning retrieval workflows.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for convergence, overfitting, and slow training.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 and AgentDB from agentic-flow.
Assumes users understand basic reinforcement learning concepts.
Provides guidance and examples; it does not train models by itself.
Uses npx examples that should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Prototype a learning agent
use_cases.description: Select a template, create a plugin, and plan a training loop for a new agent task.

use_cases.title: Add adaptive behavior to agents
use_cases.description: Store task experiences in AgentDB and retrieve learned patterns for future decisions.

use_cases.title: Compare reinforcement learning methods
use_cases.description: Review algorithm strengths and choose a method for offline, value-based, or policy-gradient experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Create my first plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AgentDB Learning Plugins to help me choose a starter template for a simple game agent. Include prerequisites and safe setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an algorithm
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Decision Transformer, Q-Learning, SARSA, and Actor-Critic for my task. Recommend one and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a training workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an AgentDB training workflow that collects experiences, trains in batches, validates results, and reports model quality.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-agent learning system
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced AgentDB learning setup for several agents sharing experiences. Include replay strategy, evaluation signals, and safety checks.

output_examples.input: I have logged expert trajectories and want offline learning.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: use Decision Transformer. It can learn from saved experiences without online exploration, then evaluate against held-out trajectories.

output_examples.input: My Q-Learning agent overfits after 50 epochs.
output: Reduce the learning rate and keep a validation split.
Compare training and validation loss before increasing epochs.
Consolidate repeated memories to reduce noisy examples.

output_examples.input: I need a plugin for continuous control.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: use Actor-Critic. It supports continuous or discrete actions and uses a value baseline to stabilize policy updates.

best_practices: Pin AgentDB package versions before running generated npx commands.
Keep training experiences free of credentials and customer secrets.
Validate learned behavior against separate evaluation data before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not run npx commands from untrusted branches without review.
Do not store raw private user data as training experiences.
Do not treat sample metrics as production readiness evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill execute training automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You choose when to run commands or training code.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What prerequisites are required?
faq.answer: You need Node.js 18 or newer, AgentDB through agentic-flow, and basic reinforcement learning knowledge.

faq.question: Which algorithm should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with Decision Transformer for logged data, Q-Learning for discrete tasks, or Actor-Critic for continuous control.

faq.question: Can it handle private training data?
faq.answer: It can describe local storage workflows, but you must remove secrets and protect database files.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production agents?
faq.answer: It can support planning and prototypes. Production use needs pinned dependencies, tests, monitoring, and safety review.
